; The POST transaction machine simulates L's commit driver (Builder P, landing 1: P4,
; AckEligible => DurableCommitEvidence for the machine).
;
; books/post-transaction.lisp is the machine (fn-ptx); books/post-transaction-durable.lisp is
; L's driver fn-ptd, whose keystone fn-ptd-posted-records-are-recovered-at-every-later-cut says
; every record fn-ptd answers :posted is recovered at every later cut.  This book maps the
; machine's completions to fn-ptd's inputs and relates the two states, so the records the machine
; answers :posted are fn-ptd's, and the keystone carries over; P6
; (fn-ptx-split-crash-images-are-entry-crash-images, books/post-transaction-crash.lisp) covers the
; cuts inside the machine's split entry write.
;
; The machine reads its message (the entry's octets, the spans of fn-ptx-spans) through the
; layer's view at each step; the environment's side is the rely (fn-ptx-rely): the octets the
; machine wrote at the head's end read back, and the message is unchanged from then on except for
; the trailer the last hashing step appends.  For layer runs the rely is NOT yet discharged (P4's
; open condition): ownership alone does not give it, since a refused layer write leaves the
; machine's advanced state in place; the discharge needs a joint invariant over the handed and
; workspace buffers, their generations, fill and capacity, and the accepted requests (landing 2).
; P4's composition is over the driver's run: that the machine's emitted writes are the split
; operations of P6 at the driver's offsets is landing 2's request/effect refinement.
(in-package "ACL2")
(include-book "post-transaction")
(include-book "post-transaction-crash")
(set-verify-guards-eagerness 0)
; The proofs below run in the machine's theory as of its P5 statement: the machine book's later
; proof lemmas (P0, P3) and the crash book's rules stay disabled here unless a hint names them.
(local (in-theory (current-theory 'fn-ptx-p5)))

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; The message and the record.

; The entry's head: the frame header (fixed length) and the chain field.
(defun fn-ptx-ptd-phase (ph)
  (case ph ((:idle :reading :hashing) :ready) (:extending :extending) (:extsyncing :extsyncing)
    ((:payload-writing :log-writing) :writing) (:committing :syncing) (:fenced :fenced) (otherwise nil)))
(defun fn-ptx-kd-before-take (ks)
  (fn-ptx-kd-mk (len (fn-lgk-committed ks)) (fn-lgk-last ks) (fn-lgk-frontier ks)
                (- (fn-lgk-next-txid ks) 1) (fn-lgk-acked ks)))
(defun fn-ptx-simp (m ptd id inc fn-rtc-st)
  (declare (xargs :stobjs fn-rtc-st))
  (let* ((ph (fn-ptx-ph m)) (pph (fn-ptd-ph ptd)) (ks (fn-ptd-ks ptd)))
    (and (equal pph (fn-ptx-ptd-phase ph))
         (case pph
           (:ready (and (equal (fn-ptx-kd m) (fn-ptx-kd-of ks))
                        (equal (fn-ptd-ext ptd) (fn-ptx-ext m))
                        (not (consp (fn-lgk-batch ks))) (not (consp (fn-lgk-inflight ks)))
                        (not (equal (fn-lgk-phase ks) :fault))
                        (equal (fn-lgk-acked ks) (len (fn-lgk-committed ks)))
                        (true-listp (fn-lgk-committed ks))
                        (implies (equal ph :hashing) (fn-ptx-hash-invp m id inc fn-rtc-st))))
           (:fenced t)
           (otherwise
            (let ((w (fn-ptx-message m id inc fn-rtc-st)))
              (and (equal (fn-ptx-kd m) (fn-ptx-kd-before-take ks))
                   (equal (fn-lgk-acked ks) (len (fn-lgk-committed ks)))
                   (true-listp (fn-lgk-committed ks))
                   (<= 1 (fn-lgk-next-txid ks))
                   (equal (fn-ptd-ext ptd) (fn-ptx-ext m))
                   (equal (fn-ptd-nxt ptd) (fn-ptx-nxt m))
                   (equal (fn-ptd-rec ptd) (fn-ptx-record m id inc fn-rtc-st))
                   (equal (fn-rtc-get 1 (fn-ptx-hs m)) (fn-lg-last-trailer (list (fn-ptd-rec ptd)) (fn-lgk-last ks)))
                   (equal (append w (fn-bs-zeros (nfix (fn-rtc-get 2 (fn-ptx-hs m)))))
                          (fn-lg-log (list (fn-ptd-rec ptd)) (fn-lgk-last ks) (fn-ptx-unit m)))
                   (if (equal pph :syncing)
                       (and (equal (fn-lgk-phase ks) :appended)
                            (equal (fn-lgk-inflight ks) (list (fn-ptd-rec ptd)))
                            (not (consp (fn-lgk-batch ks))))
                     (and (equal (fn-lgk-batch ks) (list (fn-ptd-rec ptd)))
                          (fn-lg-append-admitsp ks (fn-ptx-unit m) (fn-ptd-nxt ptd)))))))))))

; The rely (the environment's side): across a step into the hashing phase the message is octets
; and its head reads back as written (all of it: the frame header of its length, the chain field); across a
; step within the hashing phase, or within the log phases, the message is unchanged; across the
; step that ends the hashing, the message gains exactly its trailer.
(defun fn-ptx-in-flight-p (ph) (member-eq ph '(:extending :extsyncing :payload-writing :log-writing :committing)))
(defun-nx fn-ptx-rely (m m2 id inc st st2)
  (let ((ph (fn-ptx-ph m)) (ph2 (fn-ptx-ph m2)))
    (and (implies (and (equal ph2 :hashing) (not (equal ph :hashing)))
                  (let ((w2 (fn-ptx-message m2 id inc st2)))
                    (and (fn-cbor-octet-listp w2)
                         (<= (fn-ptx-head-len) (len w2))
                         (equal (take (fn-ptx-head-len) w2)
                                (append (fn-ptx-frame-header (- (len w2) (fn-ptx-head-len)))
                                        (fn-ptx-kd-last (fn-ptx-kd m2)))))))
         (implies (and (equal ph2 :hashing) (equal ph :hashing))
                  (equal (fn-ptx-message m2 id inc st2) (fn-ptx-message m id inc st)))
         (implies (fn-ptx-in-flight-p ph2)
                  (if (fn-ptx-in-flight-p ph)
                      (equal (fn-ptx-message m2 id inc st2) (fn-ptx-message m id inc st))
                    (equal (fn-ptx-message m2 id inc st2)
                           (append (fn-ptx-message m id inc st) (fn-rtc-get 1 (fn-ptx-hs m2)))))))))

; The answer a machine step gives its current post, against the driver's.
(defun fn-ptx-code-of-ptd (ans)
  (and (consp ans) (case (car (car ans)) (:posted 0) (:refused 1) (:uncertain 2) (otherwise nil))))

; P4-1, the simulation step: from a related state, the driver stepped on the mapped inputs stays
; related, and an answer the driver gives is the machine's to its current post, for the same record.
(defun-nx fn-ptx-p4-1 (m ptd ev st st2 q fo ino id inc)
  (mv-let (m2 reqs c) (fn-ptx-step m ev st q)
    (declare (ignore c))
    (mv-let (ptd2 acts ans ops)
        (fn-ptd-run ptd (fn-ptx-ptd-ins m ev m2 (fn-ptx-record m2 id inc st2) fo)
                    ino (fn-ptx-unit m) (fn-ptx-fmax m))
      (declare (ignore acts ops))
      (implies (and (fn-ptx-okp m) (not (equal (fn-ptx-ph m) :closed))
                    (fn-ptx-simp m ptd id inc st)
                    (fn-ptx-rely m m2 id inc st st2)
                    (equal (fn-rtc-ev-id ev) id) (equal (fn-rtc-ev-inc ev) inc))
               (and (fn-ptx-simp m2 ptd2 id inc st2)
                    (implies (consp ans)
                             (and (equal (fn-ptx-cur-code m reqs) (fn-ptx-code-of-ptd ans))
                                  (equal (cdr (car ans)) (fn-ptx-record m id inc st)))))))))

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Traces.  A trace is a list of steps (EV ST Q FO): the event, the machine's view at it (the
; layer's view-state of its slot), the quantum, and the host's outcome were a log action to fail.
; ST2 of a step is the next step's ST (the view at the following event); the last step's is its own.
(defun-nx fn-ptx-trace-run (m trace id inc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (len trace) :hints (("Goal" :in-theory (union-theories '(len o< o-finp o-p natp (:type-prescription len) (:compound-recognizer natp-compound-recognizer)) (theory 'minimal-theory))))))
  ; (mv m-final ptd-inputs posted-records): the records of the machine's answers of code 0, in order
  (if (atom trace)
      (mv m nil nil)
    (let* ((x (car trace)) (ev (nth 0 x)) (st (nth 1 x)) (q (nth 2 x)) (fo (nth 3 x))
           (st2 (if (consp (cdr trace)) (nth 1 (cadr trace)) st)))
      (mv-let (m2 reqs c) (fn-ptx-step m ev st q)
        (declare (ignore c))
        (mv-let (mf ins posted) (fn-ptx-trace-run m2 (cdr trace) id inc)
          (mv mf
              (append (fn-ptx-ptd-ins m ev m2 (fn-ptx-record m2 id inc st2) fo) ins)
              (if (equal (fn-ptx-cur-code m reqs) 0)
                  (cons (fn-ptx-record m id inc st) posted)
                posted)))))))
(defun-nx fn-ptx-trace-relies-p (m trace id inc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (len trace) :hints (("Goal" :in-theory (union-theories '(len o< o-finp o-p natp (:type-prescription len) (:compound-recognizer natp-compound-recognizer)) (theory 'minimal-theory))))))
  ; the rely at every step, and every event the machine's own slot's
  (if (atom trace) t
    (let* ((x (car trace)) (ev (nth 0 x)) (st (nth 1 x)) (q (nth 2 x))
           (st2 (if (consp (cdr trace)) (nth 1 (cadr trace)) st))
           (m2 (mv-nth 0 (fn-ptx-step m ev st q))))
      (and (equal (fn-rtc-ev-id ev) id) (equal (fn-rtc-ev-inc ev) inc)
           (fn-ptx-rely m m2 id inc st st2)
           (fn-ptx-trace-relies-p m2 (cdr trace) id inc)))))

; The kernel the open hands the machine: L's open kernel (no batch, nothing in flight, every
; committed record acknowledged) that is not faulted.  The open's kernel is one
; (fn-ptx-open-kernelp-of-the-open: fn-lgk-recover leaves :ready), and the relation carries
; "not faulted" through every phase but :fenced (fn-ptx-related-kernel-is-faulted-only-fenced), so
; while unfenced the machine is never related to a faulted kernel.  Without it P4-2 is false: a kernel in
; :fault with no batch is fn-ptd-open-kernelp and R-related to the same store (neither reads the
; phase), fn-ptd-begin refuses its take, and the machine, whose projection fn-ptx-kd-of reads no
; phase, posts.
(defun fn-ptx-open-kernelp (ks)
  (and (fn-ptd-open-kernelp ks) (not (equal (fn-lgk-phase ks) :fault))))

; P4-2 (KEYSTONE, AckEligible => DurableCommitEvidence for the machine): from the machine the open
; admits over L's open (KS0 related to BS), along any trace that keeps the rely, the records the
; machine answered :posted are exactly fn-ptd's posted records over the mapped inputs, in order.
;   (implies (and (fn-lgk-relp bs ks0 ino genesis max) (fn-ptx-open-kernelp ks0)
;                 (equal ext (len (fn-bs-durable-content bs ino)))
;                 (equal geo (list (fn-bs-unit bs) max hmax))
;                 (fn-ptx-okp (fn-ptx-opened (fn-ptx-kd-of ks0) ext geo))
;                 (fn-ptx-trace-relies-p (fn-ptx-opened (fn-ptx-kd-of ks0) ext geo) trace id inc))
;            (mv-let (mf ins posted) (fn-ptx-trace-run (fn-ptx-opened (fn-ptx-kd-of ks0) ext geo) trace id inc)
;              (declare (ignore mf))
;              (equal posted
;                     (fn-ptd-posted (mv-nth 2 (fn-ptd-run (fn-ptd-init ks0 ext) ins ino (fn-bs-unit bs) max))))))

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Proofs (Builder P): the message, the digest's held state, the trailer and the entry.
; The held stack over whole windows is the binary-counter stack of their subtree outputs
; (fn-ptx-absorb-is-the-stack), the trailer is BLAKE3 of the message
; (fn-ptx-trailer-is-the-digest), and the message with its trailer and padding is the log of
; its record (fn-ptx-entry-of-message).

(defun-nx fn-ptx-trace-run (m trace id inc)

  ; (mv m-final ptd-inputs posted-records): the records of the machine's answers of code 0, in order
  (if (atom trace)
      (mv m nil nil)
    (let* ((x (car trace)) (ev (nth 0 x)) (st (nth 1 x)) (q (nth 2 x)) (fo (nth 3 x))
           (st2 (if (consp (cdr trace)) (nth 1 (cadr trace)) st)))

           (st2 (if (consp (cdr trace)) (nth 1 (cadr trace)) st))

      (and (equal (fn-rtc-ev-id ev) id) (equal (fn-rtc-ev-inc ev) inc)

; fn: the POST machine's acceptance spans PRE, INS and SUFTAIL bounded by one
; term K of the sealed configuration (books/post-transaction.lisp
; fn-ptx-acc-end, lane/post, Builder P: |pre|, |ins|, |suftail| <= K).  The
; record's head and tail around the payload are bounded by the records seam
; (books/records-seam.lisp: head <= *fn-record-head-max-octets*, tail <=
; *fn-record-tail-max-octets*); the injected block the head span carries is
; bounded by C's O1 figure (books/filed-stored.lisp
; fn-o1-injected-block-octets, 2236 + 2 len(agent)) at the widest agent a
; configuration admits (books/injection.lisp fn-inj-configp:
; len(agent) <= *fn-inj-max-agent-octets*).  K is derived from those figures,
; never pinned.

(in-package "ACL2")
(include-book "filed-stored")
(include-book "records-seam")

; The injected block at the widest agent a configuration admits.
(defun fn-adm-injected-block-max ()
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (fn-o1-injected-block-octets
   (make-list *fn-inj-max-agent-octets* :initial-element 0)))

; KEYSTONE: an agent within the configuration's bound injects at most
; (fn-adm-injected-block-max) octets.
(defthm fn-adm-injected-block-within-its-max
  (implies (<= (len agent) *fn-inj-max-agent-octets*)
           (<= (fn-o1-injected-block-octets agent) (fn-adm-injected-block-max)))
  :rule-classes :linear
  :hints (("Goal" :in-theory (enable fn-o1-injected-block-octets))))

; Every configuration's own agent meets the hypothesis.
(defthm fn-adm-configured-injected-block-within-its-max
  (implies (fn-inj-configp config)
           (<= (fn-o1-injected-block-octets (fn-inj-config-agent config))
               (fn-adm-injected-block-max)))
  :rule-classes :linear
  :hints (("Goal" :in-theory (e/d (fn-inj-configp) (fn-o1-injected-block-octets
                                                     fn-adm-injected-block-max))
                  :use ((:instance fn-adm-injected-block-within-its-max
                                   (agent (fn-inj-config-agent config)))))))

; K: the widest acceptance span, the record's head with the injected block,
; or its tail.
(defun fn-adm-acc-out-max ()
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (max (+ *fn-record-head-max-octets* (fn-adm-injected-block-max))
       *fn-record-tail-max-octets*))

(defthm fn-adm-acc-out-max-holds-the-head-and-the-block
  (<= (+ *fn-record-head-max-octets* (fn-adm-injected-block-max))
      (fn-adm-acc-out-max))
  :rule-classes nil)

(defthm fn-adm-acc-out-max-holds-the-tail
  (<= *fn-record-tail-max-octets* (fn-adm-acc-out-max))
  :rule-classes nil)

;;; SubmissionTaken (books/owner-results.lisp fn-ores-take-result): WORD
;;; (:idle, :taken, :taken-control, :taken-transit), the submission's ID,
;;; MSGID, stored OCTETS and GROUPS, checked once by the recognizer (the
;;; octet fields are octet lists, the groups lists of them); read here.
(defun fnn-owner-take ()
  ;; fnn-owner-result's check, written out: the entry is dispatched through
  ;; fnn-owner-core, where the host reading (tools/harness_check.py) sees it
  ;; and definterface declares it (lane post-guard-off).
  (let ((value (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-take)))
    (unless (fnn-core 'fn-ores-submission-taken-p value)
      (fnn-fault "owner returned a malformed result from ~(~a~)" 'fn-owner-take))
    value))

(defun fnn-owner-taken-word (taken)
  (fnn-core 'fn-ores-taken-word taken))

(defun fnn-owner-taken-id (taken)
  (fnn-core 'fn-ores-taken-id taken))

(defun fnn-owner-taken-msgid (taken)
  (fnn-octets (fnn-core 'fn-ores-taken-msgid taken)))

(defun fnn-owner-taken-octets (taken)
  (fnn-octets (fnn-core 'fn-ores-taken-octets taken)))

(defun fnn-owner-taken-groups (taken)
  (mapcar #'fnn-octets (fnn-core 'fn-ores-taken-groups taken)))

(defun fnn-owner-refresh-compression (log)
  "The log's compression threshold from the owner's live configuration
(fn-owner-compress-min-octets: the `compress-min-octets' row, 0 off), read
where the batch bounds are read, so a reconfiguration applies from the next
record on (lane compression-extents-2)."
  (when log
    (setf (fnn-log-lz-min log) (fnn-nat (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-compress-min-octets)))))

(defun fnn-owner-publish-prepared (service label)
  "Publish and finish the one ACL2-prepared owner transaction."
  (let* ((store (fnn-owner-service-store service))
         (record (fnn-core-arena-state 'fn-owner-pending-octets))
         ;; The file is named from the staged record's own sequence, ACL2's
         ;; (fn-sbud-pending-sequence); the host keeps no count of its own.
         (sequence (fnn-pending-sequence
                    (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-pending-sequence))))
    (unless (fnn-octet-list-p record)
      (fnn-fault "owner returned malformed ~a transaction" label))
    (when (fnn-store-logp store) (fnn-owner-refresh-compression (fnn-store-log store)))
    (handler-case
        (fnn-publish store sequence (fnn-octets record))
      (fnn-store-indeterminate (e) (error e))
      (fnn-store-fault (e)
        ; A structural/core fault is never a capacity refusal.  Preserve the
        ; fence and propagate it to the service fault boundary.
        (setf (fnn-store-fenced store) t)
        (error e))
      (fnn-store-error (e)
        (unless (fnn-store-fenced store)
          (setf (fnn-store-fenced store) t)
          (unless (eq (fnn-owner-action 'fn-owner-known-abort) :aborted)
            (fnn-indeterminate "owner rejected known ~a abort" label))
          ; A known pre-publication refusal consumed the reservation.  It is
          ; the only error branch that reopens the writer without recovery.
          (setf (fnn-store-fenced store) nil))
        (error e)))
    (setf (fnn-store-fenced store) t)
    (fnn-finish store)
    ;; PRF-252: the committed delta wakes the consumer waits.
    (fnn-owner-signal-commit service)
    :durable))

(defun fnn-owner-preflight-publication (service kind)
  "Ask the owner whether one more record of KIND fits the Store's budget.

ACL2 decides it from the profile it was handed at open and the count of the
Store it carries (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-publication-verdict); the
host holds no count and no bound of its own here.  An article is not asked
here: its budget is part of its prepare (fn-owner-prepare)."
  (declare (ignore service))
  (unless (eq (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-publication-verdict kind) :admissible)
    (fnn-refuse "Store transaction budget refuses ~(~a~) transaction" kind))
;;; fn-lb-owner-gate through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate-buffer): under
;;; `posting-policy bound-logins' a bound login's article that is unsigned, or
;;; signed by another principal, is refused with the gate's reason
;;; (:login-unsigned, :login-not-bound) before any Store call; every other
;;; verdict continues into the unchanged attempt.  The verdict's log line
;;; names the login.
(defun fnn-owner-attempt-served (service msgid payload groups evidence)
  (setq *fnn-owner-transit-detail* nil
        *fnn-owner-transit-verdict* nil)
  ;; D27 (sweep S002): the buffer is filled once, here, and the gate and the
  ;; attempt read it (fn-owner-login-gate-buffer, fnn-owner-attempt-filled).
  (fnn-octets-fill payload)
  (let ((gate (fnn-core-buffer-state 'fn-owner-login-gate-buffer)))
    (unless (and (consp gate) (member (first gate) '(:pass :refused)))
      (fnn-fault "owner returned malformed login gate ~a" gate))
    (fnn-owner-log 'fn-owner-login-log-line t)
    (let ((word (if (eq (first gate) :refused)
                    (fnn-owner-transit-refused gate)
                  (fnn-owner-attempt-filled service msgid payload groups
                                            evidence))))
      (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-served-post-word word
                      *fnn-owner-transit-detail*))))

(defun fnn-owner-retention-commit (service event)
  "Publish one ACL2-authored retention event through the normal Store path."
  (unless (and (listp event) (= (length event) 5)
               (member (first event) '(:undertake :release))
               (stringp (second event)) (stringp (third event))
               (stringp (fourth event)) (integerp (fifth event)))
    (fnn-fault "ACL2 returned malformed Store retention event"))
  (let ((store (fnn-owner-service-store service)))
    (fnn-owner-preflight-publication service (first event))
    (let ((*fnn-observe-callback* #'fnn-owner-observe)
                (*fnn-identity-reservation-callback* #'fnn-owner-identity-reservation)
          (*fnn-finish-callback* #'fnn-owner-finish))
      ;; The exact ACL2-authored event funds its reserved release identity
      ;; and produces the one-shot capability consumed by preparation.
      (fnn-advance-frontier store
                            (fnn-nat (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-next-txid)) event)
      (let ((prepared
             (fnn-owner-action
              'fn-owner-prepare-retention (first event)
              (fnn-octet-list (fnn-string-octets (second event)))
              (fnn-octet-list (fnn-string-octets (third event)))
              (fnn-octet-list (fnn-string-octets (fourth event)))
              (fifth event))))
        (unless (eq prepared :prepared)
          (unless (eq (fnn-owner-action 'fn-owner-refuse-reservation) :refused)
            (fnn-indeterminate "owner could not consume refused retention reservation"))
          (fnn-refuse "canonical Store refused retention event")))
      (fnn-owner-publish-prepared service "retention"))))

(defun fnn-owner-identity-commit (service event)
  "Publish one ACL2-constructed keyring snapshot or atomic acceptance event."
  (let ((store (fnn-owner-service-store service)))
    ;; ACL2's verdict over the event itself (host/owner-host.lisp
    ;; fn-owner-identity-publication-verdict): a composite is charged its
    ;; figure, then the memory gate over the row it stages; the refusal
    ;; names the verdict's word (:memory among them).
    (let ((verdict (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-identity-publication-verdict event)))
      (unless (eq verdict :admissible)
        (error 'fnn-identity-verdict-refusal
               :word verdict
               :message (format nil "Store refuses ~(~a~) transaction (~(~a~))"
                                (fnn-core 'fn-wire-event-kind event) verdict))))
    (let ((*fnn-observe-callback* #'fnn-owner-observe)
                (*fnn-identity-reservation-callback* #'fnn-owner-identity-reservation)
          (*fnn-finish-callback* #'fnn-owner-finish))
      (fnn-advance-frontier store
                            (fnn-nat (fnn-owner-core 'fn-owner-next-txid)))
      ;; The entry stages the interned row and reads the arena only; when
      ;; the Store took a composite it names the article's payload and the
      ;; host seals exactly those octets (host/owner-host.lisp
      ;; fn-owner-prepare-identity, books/owner-identity-intern.lisp).
      (let ((prepared (fnn-core-arena-state 'fn-owner-prepare-identity event)))
        (when (and (consp prepared) (eq (first prepared) :seal))

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. P7 (POST landing 2) seam question for A18: the process has one fn-rtc-st, and both your lease layer fn-hll (machine fn-hlm-step, books/runtime-contract-host-lease.lisp) and my POST layer fn-ptl (machine fn-ptx-step, books/post-transaction-layer.lisp) are whole-pool layers: each layer's invp and x-step read every slot's mstate with its own machine, so the host cannot run fn-hll-x-step and fn-ptl-x-step over the same stobj without breaking both invariants.
My proposal: one product layer for the process, its machine dispatching on the slot (static slot 1 = fn-ptx-step, connection slots = your fn-hlm-step plus the poster's hand of its article buffer), defined by fn-rtc-def-layer in a new book I write (books/post-transaction-host-layer.lisp), with your HL keystones and my P0-P6 carried to it by lemmas that the product's step at a slot is that slot's machine (no restatement of yours). The alternative is a second congruent pool stobj for POST, which charges a second pool in M's equation; I do not want that.
Questions: (1) is the product layer acceptable to you, and do you want to own its connection-slot arm; (2) your lease's host executor (fnn-live-rtc-st in io.lisp, fnn-owner-lease-install-locked) is the install point I would extend: may host/native/post.lisp call fn-<product>-x-init there instead of fn-hld-init, once the lease lands; (3) until the lease is on dev I build against lane/vertical-lease@bf5b06f60 and name an adapter, retired by your lease READY. Your grant list from A12 (owner.lisp drain-one/take/taken-octets/publish-prepared/payload-octets and the attempt-served POST arm; io.lisp fnn-publish, fnn-log-compress, fnn-log-take-verdict, fnn-log-take, fnn-log-publish) I take as standing; I send you the lines before deleting.

# Codex worker c1 (Builder P7, POST landing 2): guard verification of the POST machine's step

## Goal
The host will execute the POST machine through its layer's executable copies, so fn-ptx-step must be
guard-verified with guard T (beyond the stobj recognizer fn-rtc-st-p that ACL2 adds), because the layer
generator calls it as the constrained `fn-rtc-mx-step`, whose signature is
`((fn-rtc-mx-step * * fn-rtc-st *) => (mv * * *))` with no guard (books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:57-68).
Then books/post-transaction-layer.lisp drops its `(set-verify-guards-eagerness 0)` so that
`fn-rtc-def-layer fn-ptl` admits the executable copies fn-ptl-x-* WITH their guards verified (the way
books/runtime-contract-host-lease.lisp's `fn-rtc-def-layer fn-hll` does for its machine).

Real signatures:
- books/post-transaction.lisp:581 `(defun fn-ptx-step (m ev fn-rtc-st q) ...)`, state accessors fn-ptx-* (fn-rtc-get),
  fn-ptx-closed (:151), fn-ptx-opened (:147). The book sets `(set-verify-guards-eagerness 0)` after its includes.
- The constrained acceptance fn-ptx-acc-* (encapsulate at books/post-transaction.lisp ~:57); give the
  encapsulate's signatures guard T only if needed and only by adding `:guard t` style declarations to the
  local witnesses and signatures; NO constraint (defthm inside the encapsulate) changes.
- L's driver functions in books/post-transaction-durable.lisp are L's file: do NOT edit it. If fn-ptx-step
  calls a function whose guards are unverified there, add `(verify-guards <fn>)` events in
  books/post-transaction.lisp (before the first use), with whatever local lemmas they need.

## What you may change
- books/post-transaction.lisp: add `(declare (xargs :guard ...))`, `:guard-hints`, `mbe`/`mbt` ONLY where the
  :logic is the existing body verbatim, `verify-guards` events, and new local lemmas. Every existing defun's
  BODY and every existing defthm/defun-sk/defun-nx's statement stays byte-identical. Prefer guard T on every
  function the step reaches; a non-T guard on a callee is fine when the caller establishes it.
- books/post-transaction-layer.lisp: remove line 20's eagerness setting and the five verify-guards lines if they
  become redundant; nothing else, unless the generator's guard proofs need a hint in the existing :hints form,
  in which case extend only those hints.
- books/post-transaction-sim.lisp, books/post-transaction-crash.lisp, tests/acl2/post-transaction-tests.lisp: only
  if a guard addition breaks one of their proofs; then only hints, never a statement.
- Scratch: build/post-runs/l2/c1/ (logs, notes, your report).

## Gate (exact)
    cd /Users/ember/dev/fn/build/lanes/post
    timeout 900 python3 tools/proof_repl.py start pc1 books/post-transaction     # iterate here; session names start pc1
    timeout 300 python3 tools/proof_repl.py send pc1 '(verify-guards fn-ptx-step)' --limit 120
Then once at the end, detached with a PID file, log in build/post-runs/l2/c1/certify.log:
    timeout 5400 python3 tools/certify_books.py --incremental --jobs 4 --no-publish books/post-transaction books/post-transaction-crash books/post-transaction-sim books/post-transaction-layer tests/acl2/post-transaction-tests
It must pass, and in a REPL over books/post-transaction-layer both of these must hold:
    (guard-verified-p 'fn-ptx-step (w state))  =>  T
    (guard-verified-p 'fn-ptl-x-step (w state)) =>  T
Do NOT load books/post-transaction-crash from source after the machine book (rewriter loop): include it certified.

## Do not
skip-proofs, defaxiom, a ttag, `:verify-guards nil` left on anything the step reaches, any change to an existing
theorem statement or definition body, editing any other file, git commit/push/stash/reset/checkout (git is
read-only for you, `git -C /abs/path` only), opening anything outside /Users/ember/dev/fn/build/lanes/post,
reading personal files or any LANEDUMP.md, launching anything on hbox or persvati, make, any test suite.
No foreground wait over 60 s; `timeout` on every command.

## Report (build/post-runs/l2/c1/REPORT.md, ten lines or fewer, and as your final message)
The guards added (which functions got a non-T guard and why), new lemmas and verify-guards events, the certify
verdict and its log path, the two guard-verified-p answers, anything that could not be verified and the exact
failing goal.

EOF
cat nine.txt >> c1/BRIEF.md; wc -l c1/BRIEF.md; tail -5 c1/BRIEF.md | cut -c1-80

content.text:
POST landing 2 is under way but not proved, built or gated yet. Two Codex workers are running, and I'm waiting on them before I write the statements packet.

**Lane.** The worktree `/Users/ember/dev/fn/build/lanes/post` is fast-forwarded to dev bf81a2991, the C5 train with landing 1. The copy of `tools/test_search.py` that was untracked there is now on dev; I kept the old copy as `build/post-runs/test_search.py.untracked-landing1`. Landing-2 scratch goes in `build/post-runs/l2/`.

**Seams settled** (one line went to main):
- **With A18:** the process has one `fn-rtc-st`, and A's lease layer `fn-hll` and my POST layer `fn-ptl` each cover the whole pool, so they can't share it. Agreed fix:
  - I write one combined layer in `books/post-transaction-host-layer.lisp`: static slot 1 runs `fn-ptx-step`; connection slots run A's `fn-hlm-step` plus handing the poster's article buffer to slot 1.
  - A's HL and K1-K7 keystones and its premises book carry over by lemmas, not restatement.
  - A reviews the connection-slot arm and its carry lemmas before the READY.
  - Once the lease lands I may change one hunk of `fnn-owner-lease-install-locked`, sending A the lines first.
  - Until then I build against lane/vertical-lease@0666e02e3 under a named adapter, retired by A's lease READY. A12's grant list stands.
- **With M21:**
  - I write the acceptance instance, `books/post-acceptance.lisp` (`fn-pacc-*`). It is compared against `fn-owner-prepare`'s verdict and staged record, and M audits the statement before any proof.
  - For the 552 MB term, M wants a keystone, not a census line. It should bound the bytes the POST path holds per request by the realizer's request sizes (`fn-ptx-max-reqs` and the pool buffers). M then restates `fn-heap-request-octets` over it after L-RUN-LAUNCH is filed.
- **With L:** the fault controls and boundary labels from L8 are already frozen in L's continuation, so I'm implementing them as written. No new message was needed.

**Running now:**
- **c1** (PID file `build/post-runs/l2/c1/codex.pid`, brief in the same folder): guard verification of `fn-ptx-step` with guard T. Its gate is that the layer book drops eagerness 0, `fn-ptl-x-step` comes out guard-verified, and a transitive certify of the five POST books passes on the laptop. Every statement must stay byte-identical; I'll audit that against the diff.
- **c2** (`build/post-runs/l2/c2/`): a read-only survey for the statements packet. It covers contract events and the hand, the machine's requests, P6's split operations, A's lease executor, the current POST path and its list conversions, the record build, and `fn-heap-request-octets`.

Each has a background wait that notifies me when it exits.

**A design problem before the acceptance statement can be written.** The acceptance's begin takes only a txid, and its feeds see only the head's octets. But `fn-owner-prepare` (`host/owner-host.lisp:2285`) also refuses on owner and arena state: duplicate Message-ID, handle space, budget and the memory gate. As constrained, the acceptance can't make those refusals, so a duplicate article could be written to the log. I'll settle where those checks go once c2's survey is in: either in the connection arm before the hand, or a context argument to the acceptance's begin. If it needs a change to the acceptance's constraints, I'll send main a DECISION.

**Next:**
1. Audit c1's diff.
2. Write the statements packet: the combined layer and its carry lemmas, the rely discharge for layer runs, the mapping of the machine's writes onto P6's split operations, the acceptance keystone, the hosted establishment of the seven premises (`fn-ptx-in-flight-p` included), and M's request-size keystone. Run `test_search` on each.
3. Brief Codex for the proofs and for `host/native/post.lisp`.

PRF-10007's row gets registered when the realizer gives `fn-bs-durable-content` and the other three their host caller.

## 1. Runtime contract v2.2

### Events, actions, requests, and fields

The external event is a completion `(kind id inc op outcome [data])`, admitted by `fn-rtc-completionp` (length 5 or 6); `op` participates in the outstanding-use key. `fn-rtc-e-*` read external completion fields; the machine's delivered event is `(kind outcome id inc . more)` and has no operation field. See `books/runtime-contract.lisp:298`–314 and `:1401`–1407. The `fn-rtc-ev-*` accessors found in this runtime family are `fn-rtc-ev-id`, `fn-rtc-ev-inc`, and `fn-rtc-ev-opened-data`; separate `fn-rtc-ev-kind`, `fn-rtc-ev-outcome`, `fn-rtc-ev-hand-*` definitions were not found. POST reads kind/outcome/more using `fn-rtc-get` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:515`–536).

**Source: `books/runtime-contract.lisp:289`–314. Verbatim:**

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-outcomep (o)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (and (true-listp o)
       (case (fn-rtc-get 0 o)
         ((:done :short) (and (equal (len o) 2) (natp (fn-rtc-get 1 o))))
         (:failed (equal (len o) 2))
         (:cancelled (equal (len o) 1))
         (otherwise nil))))

; (kind id inc op outcome) or, for an :in kind, (kind id inc op outcome data).
(defun fn-rtc-completionp (e)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (and (true-listp e)
       (or (equal (len e) 5) (equal (len e) 6))
       (member-eq (fn-rtc-get 0 e) *fn-rtc-kinds*)
       (natp (fn-rtc-get 1 e))
       (natp (fn-rtc-get 2 e))
       (natp (fn-rtc-get 3 e))
       (fn-rtc-outcomep (fn-rtc-get 4 e))))

(defun fn-rtc-e-id (e) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (nfix (fn-rtc-get 1 e)))
(defun fn-rtc-e-inc (e) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (nfix (fn-rtc-get 2 e)))
(defun fn-rtc-e-op (e) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (nfix (fn-rtc-get 3 e)))
(defun fn-rtc-e-outcome (e) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (fn-rtc-get 4 e))
(defun fn-rtc-e-data (e) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (fn-rtc-get 5 e))
```

**Source: `books/runtime-contract.lisp:1401`–1407. Verbatim:**

```lisp

(defun fn-rtc-ev (kind out id inc more)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (list* kind out id inc more))

(defun fn-rtc-ev-id (ev) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (nfix (fn-rtc-get 2 ev)))
(defun fn-rtc-ev-inc (ev) (declare (xargs :guard t)) (fn-rtc-get 3 ev))
```

**Source: `books/runtime-contract.lisp:1627`–1628. Verbatim:**

Vocabulary, exactly as defined:

- Completion kinds: `(:recv :send :pread :pwrite :fsync :close :accept :timer :bp-send :hand :pool :grant :extend :opened)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:120`–121).
- Worker writes buffer / `:in`: `(:recv :pread)`; worker reads buffer / `:out`: `(:send :pwrite :bp-send)` (`:123`–125). `:in` and `:out` are ownership directions, **not submit kinds**.
- Machine submit kinds: `(:recv :send :pread :pwrite :fsync :timer :bp-send :hand :pool :extend)` (`:164`–165). `:accept`, `:grant`, `:opened` are layer-issued; `:close` has its own request (`:162`).
- Action kinds are completion kinds plus `:cancel`; cancellation has no completion of its own (`:167`–169).
- Action layout is `(kind id incarnation op args)` (`:3`–7). Buffered submit emits `(kind id inc op (hd res . extra))`; unbuffered submit emits `(kind id inc op (res . extra))` (`:1121`–1140). `hd = (h g off len)` (`:29`); `res` is the slot resource.
- Ordinary extras are a list of at most two naturals below `2^64`; `:extend` alone uses exactly three naturals `(FILE FROM TO)`, all below `2^64`, `FROM < TO` (`:178`–194). The POST constructors specify the file and offset explicitly (`books/post-transaction.lisp:311`–316).

Request forms, in processing order: `(:acquire h)`, `(:write h g off octets)`, `(:release h g)`, `(:submit kind hd extra)`, `(:close)`, `(:submit :pool nil nil)`, `(:cancel kind)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:515`–527). The actual dispatch confirms these six first-word tags (`:1184`–1193). `:answer` is **not found** there or in `*fn-rtc-machine-kinds*`; POST answers via `:write` plus `:submit :hand` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:321`–326).

A refused runtime request is returned in the refused list with unchanged runtime state, no action, and a cost. For example invalid `:write` returns `(mv s nil (list r) 1)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1019`–1033); invalid submit returns `(mv s nil (list r) cost)` (`:1108`–1128). It is not an I/O failure completion. `fn-rtc-requests` continues through subsequent requests and concatenates refusals (`:1203`–1211); refusal does **not** roll back earlier successful requests, nor the machine state already installed by `fn-rtc-deliver` (`:1416`–1418). `fn-rtc-step` and `fn-rtc-x-step` discard the refused list; their starred versions retain it (`:1552`–1556; `books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:626`–630).

### Hand ownership and generation

A sender `(id inc)` submits `(:submit :hand (h g 0 n) (to tinc))` for its entire workspace. Submit requires its workspace, current generation, offset 0, length equal to fill (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1064`–1080). Ownership becomes `(:handed id inc to tinc)` at the same generation; octets are hidden from both sender and receiver while in flight (`:51`–60, `:1130`–1136).

Connections can hand only to a static slot; a static sender can hand to another slot. Target must be a different slot, at least 1 and below nslots; liveness is checked at completion (`:1088`–1100). Owner slot 1 is the POST receiver (`books/post-transaction.lisp:11`). No fixed poster slot number is baked into `fn-ptx-step`: source `fid/finc` come from event fields 4/5 (`:533`–536).

A successful matching `:hand` completion with `(:done 0)` and live target returns the buffer as the **target's workspace at generation g+1**; only the target is stepped, with `(:handed (:done 0) to tinc id inc (h (g+1) 0 fill))` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1486`–1497). On unsuccessful transfer it returns to sender or free; a live sender receives `(:hand OUT id inc new-handle)`, converting a done completion whose target is gone to `(:failed :gone)` (`:1520`–1533; ownership summary `:55`–60). The returned handle has generation g+1 (`:1525`–1526).

### View and step signatures / return shapes

**Source: `books/runtime-contract-pool-impl.lisp:476`–478. Verbatim:**

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-view-state (id inc s)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (fn-rtc-make (fn-rtc-config s) nil (fn-rtc-view id inc s) nil nil 0))
```

`fn-rtc-view-state` retains configuration and a filtered pool, with slots, uses and machine states nil and counter 0. Machines may read octets only of their workspaces and their own `:out` leases. Their own `:in` leases, handed buffers, and free home buffers retain generation/owner but hide bytes; foreign buffers become `(0 (:other) nil)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1356`–1385). `fn-rtc-deliver` passes exactly this shape (`:1412`–1415). The stobj view-reader equalities are in `books/runtime-contract-layer.lisp:14`–20.

`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1465`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-step* (s e q)
```

`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1552`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-step (s e q)
```

`books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:560`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-x-step* (e q fn-rtc-st)
```

`books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:626`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-x-step (e q fn-rtc-st)
```

`books/runtime-contract-isolation.lisp:180`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-run (s events q)
```

`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1630`:

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-init (cfg)
```

Return shapes: `fn-rtc-step*` → `(mv s2 actions refused cost)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1428`, `:1473`–1550); `fn-rtc-step` → `(mv s2 actions)` (`:1554`–1556). `fn-rtc-x-step*` → `(mv fn-rtc-st actions refused cost)`, `fn-rtc-x-step` → `(mv fn-rtc-st actions)` (`books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:560`–630); the executor mutates the abstract stobj and takes it **last**, unlike list step's state-first signature. `fn-rtc-run` → final state only; it folds `fn-rtc-step` and ignores actions (`books/runtime-contract-isolation.lisp:180`–186). `fn-rtc-init` → `(mv state actions)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1630`–1645).

### Invariant conjuncts

**Source: `books/runtime-contract.lisp:821`–844. Verbatim:**

```lisp
(defun fn-rtc-invp (s)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (let ((cfg (fn-rtc-config s)))
    (and (true-listp s) (equal (len s) 6)
         (natp (fn-rtc-get 5 s))
         (fn-rtc-configp cfg)
         (equal (len (fn-rtc-slots s)) (fn-rtc-nslots cfg))
         (fn-rtc-slots-okp 0 (fn-rtc-slots s))
         (fn-rtc-statics-okp 1 (fn-rtc-nstatic cfg) (fn-rtc-slots s))
         (equal (len (fn-rtc-pool s)) (fn-rtc-nbufs cfg))
         (fn-rtc-pool-okp 0 (fn-rtc-pool s) s)
         (fn-rtc-uses-okp (fn-rtc-uses s) s)
         (true-listp (fn-rtc-mstates s))
         (equal (len (fn-rtc-mstates s)) (fn-rtc-nslots cfg))
         (fn-rtc-mstates-okp (fn-rtc-mstates s))
         (fn-rtc-draining-okp 0 (fn-rtc-slots s) (fn-rtc-uses s))
         ;; the listener's :accept is armed exactly while a slot is free
         (iff (fn-rtc-free-slot 0 (fn-rtc-slots s))
              (fn-rtc-kind-out-p :accept 0 0 (fn-rtc-uses s)))
         ;; the listener's :grant is armed exactly while a pool buffer is
         ;; free and a request waits
         (iff (and (fn-rtc-free-pool-buf 0 (fn-rtc-pool s) cfg)
                   (fn-rtc-oldest-wait (fn-rtc-uses s)))
              (fn-rtc-kind-out-p :grant 0 0 (fn-rtc-uses s))))))
```

The named conjuncts are `fn-rtc-configp`, `fn-rtc-slots-okp`, `fn-rtc-statics-okp`, `fn-rtc-pool-okp`, `fn-rtc-uses-okp`, `fn-rtc-mstates-okp`, `fn-rtc-draining-okp`, plus the shape/length/counter clauses and iff clauses arming `:accept` when a slot is free and `:grant` when a free pool buffer and oldest wait coexist (verbatim above).

### T1–T15 names and statement scope

| ID | Name and one-line statement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `fn-rtc-init-establishes-invp`: valid config gives an invariant initial state. | `books/runtime-contract-invariant.lisp:584` |
| T2 | `fn-rtc-step-preserves-invp`: invariant state remains invariant after any step. | `books/runtime-contract-invariant.lisp:1612` |
| T3 | `fn-rtc-outstanding-use-is-leased`: a buffered outstanding use under invp names a nonrecyclable buffer at its handle generation. | `books/runtime-contract.lisp:1952` |
| T4 | `fn-rtc-outstanding-use-is-stable`: a step not ending U retains U (or grants its wait on `:grant`) and, for a handle, preserves the entire buffer. | `books/runtime-contract.lisp:2294` |
| T5 | `fn-rtc-completion-ends-its-use`: a matching completion removes U's key from `fn-rtc-end-use`'s uses. | `books/runtime-contract.lisp:1965` |
| T6 | `fn-rtc-unmatched-completion-is-discarded`: unmatched key under invp gives identical state and nil actions. | `books/runtime-contract.lisp:1943` |
| T7 | `fn-rtc-machine-changes-only-when-delivered-to`: a changed machine J implies acting completion and J equals the runtime target. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:260` |
| T8 | `fn-rtc-other-workspaces-are-untouched`: a workspace whose owner slot differs from target remains the same entire buffer. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:438` |
| T9 | `fn-rtc-generation-is-monotone`: under invp the buffer generation cannot decrease in a step. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:99` |
| T10 | `fn-rtc-every-action-is-outstanding`: each emitted action is well formed and its key exists in next uses (cancel names its underlying operation). | `books/runtime-contract-actions.lisp:312` |
| T11 | `fn-rtc-commit-only-on-own-barrier-completion`: false→true committed observer requires acting own `:fsync` completion tagged `:done`. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:330` |
| T12 | `fn-rtc-step-is-charged`: invp and natp q bound cost by q+C, number of actions, and handle-named octets. | `books/runtime-contract-budget.lisp:429` |
| T13 | `fn-rtc-end-use-retires-last`: ending the last use of a draining slot retires it to free. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:550` |
| T14 | `fn-rtc-view-hides-in-leased-bytes`: equal config and pools agreeing off in-lease bytes give equal instance views. | `books/runtime-contract-isolation.lisp:235` |
| T15 | `fn-rtc-machine-states-are-bounded`: invp and natp j bound machine size by `fn-rtc-m-max-state`. | `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:118` |

T8 covers buffers **already owned as workspace**, including ones previously delivered by hand. T4 covers outstanding hands/leases; T16b below pins an in-flight hand's only landing. These are the directly relevant protection statements, rather than a guessed theorem named “another-slot-cannot-write.”

**Source: `books/runtime-contract-keystones.lisp:438`–444. Verbatim:**

```lisp
(defthm fn-rtc-other-workspaces-are-untouched
  (implies (and (fn-rtc-invp s)
                (equal (fn-rtc-get 0 (fn-rtc-b-owner (fn-rtc-buffer h s))) :workspace)
                (not (equal (fn-rtc-get 1 (fn-rtc-b-owner (fn-rtc-buffer h s)))
                            (fn-rtc-target s e))))
           (equal (fn-rtc-buffer h (mv-nth 0 (fn-rtc-step s e q)))
                  (fn-rtc-buffer h s)))
```

Request forms, in processing order: `(:acquire h)`, `(:write h g off octets)`, `(:release h g)`, `(:submit kind hd extra)`, `(:close)`, `(:submit :pool nil nil)`, `(:cancel kind)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:515`–527). The actual dispatch confirms these six first-word tags (`:1184`–1193). `:answer` is **not found** there or in `*fn-rtc-machine-kinds*`; POST answers via `:write` plus `:submit :hand` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:321`–326).

A refused runtime request is returned in the refused list with unchanged runtime state, no action, and a cost. For example invalid `:write` returns `(mv s nil (list r) 1)` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1019`–1033); invalid submit returns `(mv s nil (list r) cost)` (`:1108`–1128). It is not an I/O failure completion. `fn-rtc-requests` continues through subsequent requests and concatenates refusals (`:1203`–1211); refusal does **not** roll back earlier successful requests, nor the machine state already installed by `fn-rtc-deliver` (`:1416`–1418). `fn-rtc-step` and `fn-rtc-x-step` discard the refused list; their starred versions retain it (`:1552`–1556; `books/runtime-contract-exec.lisp:626`–630).

### Hand ownership and generation

A sender `(id inc)` submits `(:submit :hand (h g 0 n) (to tinc))` for its entire workspace. Submit requires its workspace, current generation, offset 0, length equal to fill (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1064`–1080). Ownership becomes `(:handed id inc to tinc)` at the same generation; octets are hidden from both sender and receiver while in flight (`:51`–60, `:1130`–1136).

Connections can hand only to a static slot; a static sender can hand to another slot. Target must be a different slot, at least 1 and below nslots; liveness is checked at completion (`:1088`–1100). Owner slot 1 is the POST receiver (`books/post-transaction.lisp:11`). No fixed poster slot number is baked into `fn-ptx-step`: source `fid/finc` come from event fields 4/5 (`:533`–536).

A successful matching `:hand` completion with `(:done 0)` and live target returns the buffer as the **target's workspace at generation g+1**; only the target is stepped, with `(:handed (:done 0) to tinc id inc (h (g+1) 0 fill))` (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1486`–1497). On unsuccessful transfer it returns to sender or free; a live sender receives `(:hand OUT id inc new-handle)`, converting a done completion whose target is gone to `(:failed :gone)` (`:1520`–1533; ownership summary `:55`–60). The returned handle has generation g+1 (`:1525`–1526).

### Static slots, opened, and log write completion

Slot 0 is listener. Slots 1..nstatic are live at incarnation 1 from init and cannot be closed; owner is slot 1 (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:17`–23, `:210`–214, `:1044`–1055). `fn-rtc-init` builds listener/static/free slots, free pool, static machine initial states and empty uses, arms one `:opened` for every static slot, then rearms accept/grant (`:1601`–1645). Each opened action is `(:opened j 1 op (0))` (`:1615`–1622). External completion `(:opened j 1 op (:done 0) (KD EXT GEO))` becomes machine `(:opened (:done 0) j 1 (KD EXT GEO))`; failure/cancellation delivers `(:opened OUT j 1)` without data. Use consumption permits at most one delivery; machine cannot submit/cancel opened (`:146`–160; `books/runtime-contract-opened.lisp:45`, `:338`, `:541`).

POST uses log file ref `*fn-ptx-lfile* = 2` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:31`). Its write request is `(:submit :pwrite (h g off n) (2 pos))` (`:312`). Runtime emits `(:pwrite id inc op (hd res 2 pos))` by the buffered submit arm (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1138`–1140). A host completion is `(:pwrite id inc op (:done n))` (or short/failed/cancelled); runtime matches use, ends the lease, validates count against handle, and delivers `(:pwrite OUT id inc)` to that machine (`:871`–890, `:1476`–1479, `:1544`–1550). POST requires `:done` and exactly the span length in both write phases (`books/post-transaction.lisp:556`–567). A successful pwrite itself is **not** POST commit: final log `:fsync` tagged done is (`:568`–573). This is the model/executor delivery protocol; the current synchronous host log path in §5 does not drive ptx with these events.

### Phase/event/request table

All rows concern `fn-ptx-step1` after the wfp check. Outcome code table is `((:posted . 0) (:refused . 1) (:uncertain . 2) (:busy . 3))` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:36`–37). Timer, pwrite, fsync and extend request expressions are quoted above.

| Current phase / delivered kind | Transition and emitted requests | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `:closed`, `:opened` | On done, builds opened state from KD/EXT/GEO if wfp, fmax and 32-byte prior hash checks pass; no requests. Other opened events leave phase unchanged. | `books/post-transaction.lisp:521`–532 |
| Any, `:handed` | Source poster is `fid/finc` from fields 4/5, buffer/length from handle at field 6. Closed/fenced answers refused; idle starts reading + `(fn-ptx-timer)`; otherwise queues up to 2 waiting posts, or answers busy. | `:533`–541; `:30`; `:336`–342 |
| `:reading`, `:timer` | First read acquires two owner home workspaces and writes nine zeros to b3; each window feeds acceptance, appends suffix part via `:write`, and emits timer if continuing. At head end writes frame+chain+PRE+INS into b1 and suffix head/part/tail into b3, then timer → hashing. Refusal releases workspaces and answers. | `:409`–477 |
| `:hashing`, `:timer` | Continue digest windows + timer, or write 32-byte trailer to b3 and request extension → extending, or first span pwrite → payload-writing. Extension target ≥2^64 answers refused without log action. | `:480`–510 |
| `:extending`, `:extend` | Done → extsyncing + `(fn-ptx-fsync)`; failure → fenced/refused end. | `:545`–548 |
| `:extsyncing`, `:fsync` | Done → payload-writing k=0 + first span pwrite; failure → fenced/refused end. | `:549`–553 |
| `:payload-writing`, `:pwrite` | Whole done count only: advance k, issue next span pwrite; last span goes to log-writing. Anything else → fenced/uncertain end. | `:554`–563 |
| `:log-writing`, `:pwrite` | Whole done count → committing + log fsync; otherwise fenced/uncertain end. | `:564`–567 |
| `:committing`, `:fsync` | Done → posted end, new kernel projection, committed=t; otherwise fenced/uncertain end. | `:568`–573 |
| Any, `:hand` | Returned answer buffer (poster gone): release handle if handlep. | `:574`–577 |
| Other phase/kind | Clear per-step committed flag, no requests, cost=1. | `:518`, `:578` |

This machine receives the handed buffer as its own workspace at owner slot 1, after runtime transfer. There is no producer of the poster-side hand in this book: it **reacts** to `:handed` (`:11`, `:533`). The request sender's exact connection slot must come from composition, not a constant guessed here.

End behavior is shared: release b1 and b3 at the current view generations; answer current post by writing the one-byte outcome at offset 0 of its article buffer and handing that whole buffer back to saved fid/finc. When fenced, answer all queued posts refused; otherwise start next queued post with a timer or become idle (`:344`–367). There is no `:answer` request. `fn-ptx-codes-to` recognizes adjacent one-octet write + hand, and `fn-ptx-cur-code` selects the current buffer's code (`:695`–709).

### Static slots, opened, and log write completion

Slot 0 is listener. Slots 1..nstatic are live at incarnation 1 from init and cannot be closed; owner is slot 1 (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:17`–23, `:210`–214, `:1044`–1055). `fn-rtc-init` builds listener/static/free slots, free pool, static machine initial states and empty uses, arms one `:opened` for every static slot, then rearms accept/grant (`:1601`–1645). Each opened action is `(:opened j 1 op (0))` (`:1615`–1622). External completion `(:opened j 1 op (:done 0) (KD EXT GEO))` becomes machine `(:opened (:done 0) j 1 (KD EXT GEO))`; failure/cancellation delivers `(:opened OUT j 1)` without data. Use consumption permits at most one delivery; machine cannot submit/cancel opened (`:146`–160; `books/runtime-contract-opened.lisp:45`, `:338`, `:541`).

POST uses log file ref `*fn-ptx-lfile* = 2` (`books/post-transaction.lisp:31`). Its write request is `(:submit :pwrite (h g off n) (2 pos))` (`:312`). Runtime emits `(:pwrite id inc op (hd res 2 pos))` by the buffered submit arm (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1138`–1140). A host completion is `(:pwrite id inc op (:done n))` (or short/failed/cancelled); runtime matches use, ends the lease, validates count against handle, and delivers `(:pwrite OUT id inc)` to that machine (`:871`–890, `:1476`–1479, `:1544`–1550). POST requires `:done` and exactly the span length in both write phases (`books/post-transaction.lisp:556`–567). A successful pwrite itself is **not** POST commit: final log `:fsync` tagged done is (`:568`–573). This is the model/executor delivery protocol; the current synchronous host log path in §5 does not drive ptx with these events.

End behavior is shared: release b1 and b3 at the current view generations; answer current post by writing the one-byte outcome at offset 0 of its article buffer and handing that whole buffer back to saved fid/finc. ## 7. Request-in-flight heap figure

**Source: `books/heap-store-figure.lisp:546`–571. Verbatim:**

```lisp
; The request in flight: the record and header lists, and (lane
; chunked-body-2, B6b) the submission the committer took: the take unpacks it
; (fn-own-take-submission), its octets, groups and Message-ID as lists until
; the outcome, one at a time.  This is what a SERVING process holds for it
; (books/memory-model.lisp fn-mm-inflight): the two octet buffers are not
; held in service (the host releases both after every load and publication,
; host/native/io.lisp fnn-octets-release and fnn-octets-pub-release; memory
; landing 3+4, census m34-owner-core).
(defun fn-heap-request-octets (profile)
```lisp
; THE INSTANT: K connections open, J of them holding a large reply, S
; article slots in use, H handshakes in flight, PUBLISHING whether a
; publication runs: its live heap, and the process with the collector's room
; over it.
(defun fn-mm-need-live (profile cfg tot k j s h publishing)
  (declare (xargs :guard t))
  (+ (fn-mm-owner tot cfg)
     (* (nfix k) (fn-mm-connection-fixed profile cfg))
     (* (nfix j) (fn-mm-large-reply profile cfg))
     (fn-heap-request-octets profile)
     (* (nfix s) (fn-heap-article-reserve-octets profile))
     (* (nfix h) *fn-cbud-handshake-scratch-octets*)
     (fn-mm-cold-reads profile cfg)
     (if publishing (fn-mm-maintenance tot cfg) 0)))
```

`fn-heap-request-octets (profile)` returns scalar bytes, and charges record/header lists plus unpacked taken submission lists in service; the two retained octet buffers are excluded from this serving term. Constants: list cost 16 bytes/octet (`books/heap-store-figure.lisp:149`), header copies=3, Message-ID=250 (`:280`–281). Thus the expression is `32*(max-record + 3*max-header) + 32*(max-article + max-header + 250)`; this is arithmetic restatement of the source, not an execution or measurement.

Direct callers found: `fn-heap-store-inflight-octets` adds `2*fn-ock-capture-budget` for offline capture (`books/heap-store-figure.lisp:568`–571); `fn-mm-inflight` adds articles, TLS handshake scratch, cold reads (`books/memory-model.lisp:362`–367); `fn-mm-need-live` includes it unconditionally while separately accounting for connection/reply/article-slot/handshake/cold/maintenance terms (`:448`–457).

**Numeric value explicitly recorded at the development profile: not found** in the searched tests, planning/evidence and build files (excluding lanedumps, POST scratch/logs). The development profile definition is `(fn-bs-profile-preset 128 25165824 32768)` (`books/byte-store-frame.lisp:1051`–1052). A scalar evaluation was not run.

There is a numeric test pin for the **small preset**, not development: `tests/acl2/heap-breakdown-tests.lisp:19` selects `*fn-heap-small-profile*`; its breakdown at `:63`–64 pins inflight-lists=7,864,320 and taken-submission-lists=1,580,864. Those are the two summands of this term (see `books/heap-breakdown.lisp:53`–59), hence their test-pinned sum is 9,445,184 bytes for that small-profile breakdown, with source/figure scope, not a measured development request. The test was read only, not executed.

## Packet-use gaps and distinctions

- `fn-ptx-message` belongs to the simulation book, and `fn-ptx-split-ops*` was not found (`books/post-transaction-sim.lisp:34`; `books/post-transaction-crash.lisp:7`).
- Runtime request refusals are output-list entries with no completion; POST outcome :refused is the machine's one-byte reply code, a different level (`books/runtime-contract.lisp:1108`–1128; `books/post-transaction.lisp:36`, `:325`).
- Poster article hand producer / concrete poster machine slot is not defined by post-transaction.lisp. This book only consumes sender fields of delivered :handed; owner is static slot 1 (`books/post-transaction.lisp:11`, `:533`–536).
- ptd fourth-value host ops, ptd syscall actions, RTC handle actions, byte-store pending ops, and synchronous host calls are five different surfaces. Their bridges need named composition statements; do not substitute one signature for another (§1–§5 citations).
- Source theorem presence is not current-closure certification. The POST book's header still warns its keystones are packet statements/not certification of record (`books/post-transaction.lisp:7`–9); this survey makes no certification claim.
- The dossier eight are reproducible numbered boundaries, not an allocation census. Current served prepare's payload-list construction and log verdict/take/compression lists are additional current sites (`host/owner-host.lisp:2536`; `host/native/io.lisp:7731`, `:9425`, `:9438`).

input.summary: DECISION: where POST admission runs vs the machine
input.message:
DECISION (P7, POST landing 2): landing 1's acceptance cannot be the admission gate. fn-ptx-acc-begin takes only a txid and is fed only the head, but today's admission needs the whole body and owner state: the D25 existing test compares source octets, the carrier signature covers the source article, the subject/obligation id is a whole-payload digest, prepare counts body lines, and the budget, memory gate and handle space read the arena (Codex c2 survey, build/lanes/post/build/post-runs/l2/c2/SURVEY.md §6). The record's PRE also carries clock, charge, subject id and evidence, which a head-only acceptance cannot compute.
(a) Recommended: admission stays the owner's, run over the poster's pool buffer before the hand. The poster's connection arm runs the existing *-buffer entries under the owner mutex (login gate, existing, prepare-buffer staging the row and txid), with no payload list, deleting owner-host.lisp:2536's fn-octets-list. It writes the decision context (txid, clock, charge, subject, evidence, groups) at the buffer's front and hands the buffer. The machine's acceptance reads the context plus the head and only lays out PRE/INS/SUF. The keystone: the laid-out record = fn-record-encode of the prepared fn-sn-article-record.
Cost of (a): the machine's spans start past the context, a definition change in books/post-transaction.lisp, re-proved with byte-identical keystone statements; M re-audits the acceptance statement against the prepared record instead of the verdict.
(b) A streaming admission inside the machine: whole-body state across windows plus owner state in the stobj; much larger, and duplicates M's gate.
(c) Keep the synchronous admission and drive only the log phases through the machine: drops the leased span, keeps the lists. Not recommended.
Until you rule I keep writing the statements that do not depend on this: the product layer, the rely discharge, the request/effect refinement, premises, guards.

(defun fn-ptx-head-len () (+ (len (fn-ptx-frame-header 0)) 32))
(defun fn-ptx-message (m id inc fn-rtc-st)
  (declare (xargs :stobjs fn-rtc-st))
  (let ((spans (fn-ptx-spans m)))
    (fn-ptx-msg-range 0 (fn-ptx-spans-len spans) spans id inc fn-rtc-st)))
; The record: the message (the trailer included once hashed) less the head and the trailer.
(defun fn-ptx-record (m id inc fn-rtc-st)
  (declare (xargs :stobjs fn-rtc-st))
  (let ((w (fn-ptx-message m id inc fn-rtc-st)))
    (nthcdr (fn-ptx-head-len) (take (- (len w) 32) w))))

; The digest's held stack over the whole windows of PREFIX (fn-b3-append-window's state).
(defun fn-ptx-stack-of (prefix)
  (if (consp prefix)
      (fn-b3-stack-push-all *fn-b3-iv* 0 *fn-ptx-wexp*
                            (fn-b3-window-outs *fn-b3-iv* *fn-ptx-wexp* 0 prefix 0) nil)
    nil))

; While hashing: the message is octets, holds its whole head, which is the frame header of its
; length and the chain field, and the held stack is the digest's state over the octets absorbed.
(defun fn-ptx-hash-invp (m id inc fn-rtc-st)
  (declare (xargs :stobjs fn-rtc-st))
  (let ((w (fn-ptx-message m id inc fn-rtc-st)) (hs (fn-ptx-hs m)))
    (and (fn-cbor-octet-listp w)
         (<= (fn-ptx-head-len) (len w))
         (equal (take (fn-ptx-head-len) w)
                (append (fn-ptx-frame-header (- (len w) (fn-ptx-head-len))) (fn-ptx-kd-last (fn-ptx-kd m))))
         (equal (fn-rtc-get 1 hs) (fn-ptx-stack-of (take (nfix (fn-rtc-get 0 hs)) w))))))

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; The map: the fn-ptd inputs one machine step gives.  R is the record read after the step; FO the
; host's outcome of a failed log action (any value but :ok; the trace supplies it).
(defun fn-ptx-ptd-ins (m ev m2 r fo)
  (let ((ph (fn-ptx-ph m)) (kind (fn-rtc-get 0 ev)) (ph2 (fn-ptx-ph m2))
        (bad (if (equal fo :ok) :eio fo)))
    (cond ((and (eq ph :hashing) (member-eq ph2 '(:extending :payload-writing))) (list (list :begin r)))
          ((and (eq ph :extending) (eq kind :extend))
           (list (cons :pwrite (if (eq ph2 :extsyncing) :ok bad))))
          ((and (eq ph :extsyncing) (eq kind :fsync))
           (list (cons :fsync (if (eq ph2 :payload-writing) :ok bad))))
          ((and (eq ph :payload-writing) (eq kind :pwrite))
           (if (eq ph2 :fenced) (list (cons :pwrite bad)) nil))
          ((and (eq ph :log-writing) (eq kind :pwrite))
           (list (cons :pwrite (if (eq ph2 :committing) :ok bad))))
          ((and (eq ph :committing) (eq kind :fsync))
           (list (cons :fsync (if (fn-ptx-committedp m2) :ok bad))))
          (t nil))))

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; The relation.  Phases map; at rest the kernel projection is the driver kernel's, which has no
; batch, nothing in flight and no fault (fn-ptd-begin's take and append need all three) and has
; acknowledged every committed record (the commit's acknowledgement counts one), and while
; hashing the digest's state is the message's; in flight the projection is the kernel's before the
; take (one txid less), the extents agree, the driver's record is the machine's, the message
; with the padding is the driver's entry, and the kernel holds the record as the driver's
; invariant fn-ptd-invp has it: before the seal the batch is the record, nothing is in flight and
; the append admits it (so the kernel is not faulted); after the seal the record is in flight
; and the kernel is :appended; and the trailer the machine holds is the chain's trailer of the
; record (the commit makes it the chain head).  (Restated from Sonnet 6's counterexample: a held
; trailer other than the digest is otherwise related, and the commit then diverges from the fence.)  (Restated from the counterexample of a driver at :writing over a
; kernel with an empty batch: its two :ok completions answer :posted and commit nothing, while
; the machine commits the record.)

;    Encoding: a fixed 1-octet version, then each field as a u32 big-endian length or value, then octets.

  (and (true-listp ctx) (equal (len ctx) 6)
       (natp (nth 0 ctx))
       (fn-cbor-octet-listp (nth 1 ctx)) (<= (len (nth 1 ctx)) (fn-adm-acc-out-max))
       (fn-cbor-octet-listp (nth 2 ctx)) (<= (len (nth 2 ctx)) (fn-adm-acc-out-max))
       (natp (nth 3 ctx))
       (fn-cbor-octet-listp (nth 4 ctx)) (<= (len (nth 4 ctx)) *fn-ptx-sufhead-max*)
       (fn-cbor-octet-listp (nth 5 ctx)) (<= (len (nth 5 ctx)) (fn-adm-acc-out-max))))

; encoding's length.
(defthm fn-pctx-round-trip
  (implies (and (fn-pctx-p ctx) (< (nth 0 ctx) (expt 2 64)) (< (nth 3 ctx) (expt 2 32)))
           (equal (fn-pctx-decode (append (fn-pctx-encode ctx) rest))
                  (list t ctx (len (fn-pctx-encode ctx))))))
; KEYSTONE C2 fn-pctx-encode-bounded: (len (fn-pctx-encode ctx)) <= *fn-pctx-max* = 1 + 6*4 + 3K + 9,
; K = (fn-adm-acc-out-max).

    (implies (car d)

; the fields), the record the machine lays out is fn-record-encode of the prepared fn-sn-article-record.

  (let* ((rec (fn-sn-article-record s obs msgid (fn-pacc-stored-payload art inj) groups oid subject evidence charge))
         (ctx (fn-pctx-of-prepared s rec art inj)))
    (implies (and (fn-record-p rec) (fn-octet-listp art) (fn-pacc-injectionp inj art))
             (and (fn-pctx-p ctx)
                  (equal (nth 0 ctx) (fn-state-next-txid (fn-node-acceptance (fn-sn-node s))))
                  (equal (append (nth 1 ctx) (take (nth 3 ctx) art) (nth 2 ctx) (nthcdr (nth 3 ctx) art)
                                 (nth 4 ctx) (nth 5 ctx))
                         (fn-record-encode rec))))))

; that edits the article anywhere but one insert after a prefix, is a RED against ruling (a)'s layout):
; KEYSTONE A0 fn-pacc-stored-payload-is-one-splice: the payload the batch path stores
; (fn-apc-cl-served-payload over fn-ipp-injected-octets, books/owner-parse-carried.lisp:207-264, as
; fn-pacc-stored-payload names it) is P0 ++ art[0,ioff) ++ INS ++ art[ioff,len) for the prefix, insert and
; offset fn-pacc-splice answers.

  (implies (and (fn-octet-listp art) (fn-pacc-injectionp inj art))
           (mv-let (p0 ins ioff) (fn-pacc-splice art inj)
             (and (natp ioff) (<= ioff (len art))
                  (equal (fn-pacc-stored-payload art inj)

  (implies (not (equal ktxid (nth 0 ctx)))
           (not (mv-nth 0 (fn-pacc-end (fn-pacc-feed* (fn-pacc-begin (list ktxid ctx)) windows) blen)))))

(defun fn-pth-init () (fn-hlm-init))

; (fn-rtc-def-layer fn-pth :step fn-pth-step :init fn-pth-init :static-init fn-pth-static-init ...)
; L1 fn-pth-at-the-owner / L2 fn-pth-at-a-connection: the dispatch (rewrite rules).
; L3 carry (A reviews): every fn-hld-* executor entry A's host calls, re-generated over fn-pth (fn-phd-*),
;    keeps fn-pth-invp, and HL5 and K1-K7 hold of fn-phd-* as stated of fn-hld-* (same statements with
;    the layer's names substituted, by functional instance; none restated).  Mechanism to settle with A.
;
; =====================================================================================================
; R. The rely's discharge for layer runs (P4's open condition).  The owner's trace of a product run:
;    every event delivered to slot 1 at incarnation 1, with the view-state of slot 1 before it and the
;    host outcome FO (:ok when the completion's outcome is (:done n) with n the request's count, else the
;    outcome itself).
(defun-nx fn-pth-owner-trace (s events q) ...)   ; (ev view q fo) per delivered slot-1 event, in order
; R0 (the joint invariant's consequence, Codex 2's point): from a reachable product state the layer
; refuses none of the owner machine's requests, so no refused write leaves the machine ahead of its buffers.
(defthm fn-pth-owner-requests-are-never-refused
  (implies (and (fn-pth-reachablep s) (equal (fn-rtc-e-id e) 1))
           (not (mv-nth 2 (fn-pth-step* s e q)))))
; KEYSTONE R1 fn-pth-runs-keep-the-rely: every product run from a reachable state keeps the rely along
; the owner's trace.
(defthm fn-pth-runs-keep-the-rely
  (implies (fn-pth-reachablep s)
           (fn-ptx-trace-relies-p (fn-pth-mstate 1 s) (fn-pth-owner-trace s events q) 1 1)))
; fn-pth-reachablep: s = (fn-pth-run (mv-nth 0 (fn-pth-init cfg)) events0 q0) for a fn-rtc-configp cfg
; whose host delivers completions per A-HOST-LANDS (books/assumptions-runtime.lisp).
;
; =====================================================================================================
; E. Request/effect refinement (Codex 1's point): the machine's emitted pwrites, applied as byte-store
;    writes at the log file's inode, are P6's split operations of the entry at the driver's frontier.
; KEYSTONE E1 fn-pth-log-writes-are-the-split-ops: along the owner's trace from the open, the pwrites the
; owner emits for one post, mapped by fn-pth-pwrite-op (h g off n pos) -> (:write ino pos octets-of-span),
; are (fn-ptx-split-ops ino (fn-lgk-frontier ks) e ls) with e the entry fn-ptd writes for its record and
; ls the machine's span lengths, in emission order.
; KEYSTONE E2 fn-pth-every-cut-is-a-covered-store: every store the host's byte store passes through
; while those writes are pending (any prefix of them applied, any admissible crash image) is a store
; P6 covers: so the composition fn-ptx-posted-records-are-recovered-at-every-later-cut holds of
; fn-pth runs, not only of the driver's.

;

;    predicate of the slot-1 machine state of a reachable product state, never assuming it):
; P-okp       (implies (fn-pth-reachablep s) (fn-ptx-okp (fn-pth-mstate 1 s)))
; P-wfp       (implies (fn-pth-reachablep s) (fn-ptx-wfp (fn-pth-mstate 1 s)))
; P-simp      (implies (fn-pth-reachablep s) (fn-ptx-simp (fn-pth-mstate 1 s) (fn-pth-driver s) 1 1 (fn-pth-view 1 s)))
;             with fn-pth-driver the fn-ptd state the owner trace's mapped inputs reach from (fn-ptd-init ks0 ext)
; P-hash-invp (implies (and (fn-pth-reachablep s) (equal (fn-ptx-ph (fn-pth-mstate 1 s)) :hashing))
;                      (fn-ptx-hash-invp (fn-pth-mstate 1 s) 1 1 (fn-pth-view 1 s)))
; P-rely      R1 above.
; P-extension (fn-olr-extension-needed-p): the case condition of fn-ptx-extension-target-bounds; both cases
;             are proved, so the premise is a case split; established by a theorem over each value.
; P-admits    (implies (and (fn-pth-reachablep s) (member (fn-ptx-ph (fn-pth-mstate 1 s)) '(:payload-writing :log-writing)))
;                      (fn-lg-append-admitsp (fn-ptd-ks (fn-pth-driver s)) (fn-ptx-unit (fn-pth-mstate 1 s)) (fn-ptd-nxt (fn-pth-driver s))))
; P-in-flight fn-ptx-in-flight-p: a phase classifier, no premise content; acknowledged in the term baseline,
;             retired by naming it executable (guard-verified, c1) and cited by R1.
;
; =====================================================================================================
; M. For M21's request term (fn-heap-request-octets restated over it):
; KEYSTONE M1 fn-pth-post-holds-no-article-list: what the POST path holds per post outside the pool is
; the owner machine's state and its requests' inline octets:
(defthm fn-pth-post-request-octets-are-bounded
  (implies (natp q)
           (and (<= (fn-rtc-size (mv-nth 0 (fn-ptx-step m ev st q))) (fn-ptx-max-state))
                (<= (fn-rtc-reqs-octets (mv-nth 1 (fn-ptx-step m ev st q))) (+ q (fn-ptx-c))))))
; with fn-ptx-c and fn-ptx-max-state closed forms at fn-ptx-acc-out-max = 2782 (a ground evaluation
; theorem); the article and the context stay in the pool buffer, charged in the pool term.  The host fact
; beside it: the realizer builds no list of the article or record (host_check / a grep gate over
; host/native/post.lisp for fnn-octet-list, coerce, fn-octets-list), and the eight conversions plus
; owner-host.lisp:2536 are deleted on the POST path.
;

; T. Teeth for P4-2 and its composition (coordinator ruling (a) of 10-11): defteeth :instances over the
; acceptance A above (attached): a ground posting trace of fn-pth from init with one prepared post, the
; removals of each hypothesis, and a mutation (the acceptance with ok forced NIL) that the claim catches;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run one ACL2 `test?` counterexample search and say what it actually did.
`test?` prints "Test? succeeded. No counterexamples were found." when it never
tested anything: for a conjecture over a function that takes a stobj (or a
constrained function without an attachment) Cgen skips testing completely and
says so only in its verbose output (P6 on hbox, 2026-10-11: fn-ptx-step and
the rest).  It also reports "proved" for a conjecture whose hypotheses no
generated example satisfied.  Most of fn's keystones are over stobjs, so the
final "Test?" line is not evidence of a search (COUNTEREXAMPLE rule 6.6).
This runs `test?` at verbosity level 3, reads Cgen's own summary, and prints
exactly one line:
    SEARCHED <m> examples 0 counterexamples (<n> tested, <u> unique)   exit 0
    COUNTEREXAMPLE <first binding>                                     exit 1
    SKIPPED <reason>                                                   exit 2
It never prints SEARCHED unless Cgen's summary says at least one example
satisfied the hypotheses and none falsified the conclusion.  The full verbose
transcript is written to --log (default: a fresh file under
build/test-search/) and its path goes to stderr.
    python3 tools/test_search.py --book books/heap-figure \\
        '(implies (natp x) (<= 0 (fnn-figure x)))'

(`acl2_slots.apply_box_defaults`), and runs under the tree's slot pool with the
certification environment.  acl2s/cgen must be certified for that launcher
(hbox: planning/hbox-acl2s-cgen-2026-10-11.md).

content.text:
c4's run of the acceptance definitions came back with a RED, but I traced it to my own brief, not to the machine's constraint. I've resumed c4 with a fix that leaves the constraint untouched. Nothing is proved yet: searches come first.

**What c4 found.** In `books/post-acceptance.lisp`, six of the seven acceptance constraints prove with their bodies unchanged. The seventh, feed-bounded, fails: it requires every feed result's size to stay within `fn-pacc-max-state` for any input state. My brief had the feed return its input state unchanged, so an oversized state stays oversized. c4's counterexample is 16,727 zero octets fed in, giving a state of size 33,455.

**The fix.** The feed and the end now pass their state through a normalizer. It keeps a state only if it has the shape `fn-pacc-begin` produces, and otherwise turns it into nil, which ends as a refusal. The machine only ever feeds the state that begin produced, so behaviour on reachable states doesn't change. c4 re-runs the ground file and the certify, and must prove the feed-bounded constraint with its body unchanged.

**Evidence so far** (one real two-group post, `build/post-runs/l2/c4/ground.out`):
- **A0, the stored payload as one splice:** equal to the batch path's stored payload. The injection is one Path insert after a prefix made of the Cancel-Lock lines and the injected header block, matching the layout ruling (a) assumed.
- **A1 and A3, the laid-out record and the batch path's published octets:** the comparison as stated can't be evaluated, because the record codec is constrained and not attached in this book. The same comparisons against the concrete encoder `fn-record-encode-impl` are both equal at every index.
- **The batch path's composition:** `fn-pacc-batch-record-octets` is non-executable (a `defun-nx` over the arena), so A3's teeth will need a real prepared post run through the image.

**Waiting:**
- c4's fix, behind a background wait.
- The hbox counterexample searches for the context-format keystones C1–C3, which start when hbox's load drops below 20.

Committed on lane/post: 9ddd948d4, the guard verification, and 7bc3f3d6b, a comment fix.
